subject: OmniRetail latency surge — fallback decision & customer note
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:03 +0000
Subject: [ALERT] EU p95 up / throughput down — OmniRetail impact

Team,

We are seeing a sustained p95 latency increase for OmniRetail traffic in eu-west-1 starting ~09:08 UTC after a routine model variant rollout. Summary:

- Impact: OmniRetail's gen-api p95 jumped from ~340ms to ~1.9s; overall QPS for that customer fell ~28% (requests queued, timeouts visible).
- Window: spike began ~09:08 UTC, error/timeout rate peaked ~09:15.
- Initial triage: autoscaler did not add capacity (backpressure from token queue), and KV cache hit-rate dropped sharply after the deploy.

Actions taken so far:
- Rolled back the new variant in the host pool at 09:22 UTC (no immediate improvement).
- Triggered manual routing to healthy pool (partial relief for other tenants).
- Collected snapshots (attached incident_snapshot_omni_1028.pdf) and timeframe logs (OPS-4512).

Open asks for product/leadership:
1) Approve a temporary routing exception to direct OmniRetail traffic to the dedicated stable-quantized variant (variant-q1) while we stabilize. This requires product to accept a short-term quality tradeoff.
2) Approve an SLA/credit escalation for the customer if we confirm >2 hours of degraded p95. Sales/CS will coordinate amount, but we need an approval path.

Requesting decision and prioritized actions — unless we get a fast approval for fallback and cache priming, the window will persist.

Karthik
SRE

[attachment: incident_snapshot_omni_1028.pdf (pdf)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:28:47 +0000
Subject: Re: [ALERT] EU p95 up / throughput down — OmniRetail impact

Thanks Karthik — good rundown. Short answers / asks:

- Product decision: I sign off on a routing exception to variant-q1 for up to 4 hours as an emergency measure, with the explicit condition that we document customer-visible quality delta and revert once p95 stabilizes.
- Engineering asks: please run an aggressive KV cache priming (prefix warm) for OmniRetail keys and enable continuous batching at a lower latency-target for that tenant while routed to q1.
- Sales/CS: Marissa, propose a temporary goodwill credit (5% of October usage) in the draft below; confirm if that aligns with escalation policy or needs exec approval.

Please action in this order:
1) Karthik: enable routing exception + cache priming now (if you can, note exact timestamp in the thread).
2) Soojin: surface any blocker from runtime (kernel/quant path) that would prevent q1 serving.
3) Marissa: prepare customer note and hold off sending until we have stabilization metrics.

I will escalate to Ops leadership if we exceed the 4-hour exception window. Keep the thread tight — only essential replies.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:36:10 +0000
Subject: Re: [ALERT] EU p95 up / throughput down — OmniRetail impact

Grace — thanks. Quick PS from CS/sales perspective:

- Customer profile: OmniRetail (large retail platform) is sensitive to checkout latency spikes; they will escalate to procurement if this impacts holiday traffic.
- Credit ask: I recommend offering 5% usage credit for October as a gesture; anything above 5% needs VP approval.
- Messaging: I drafted a short, transparent note (see attachment customer-draft-omni-1028.txt). Key points: apology, what we did, immediate mitigations, next steps, and proposed credit.

Operationally: please confirm fallback and timestamp — we will not send to customer until metrics indicate p95 trending below 600ms for 30 minutes. Also logging and postmortem deliverable should be shared by EOD today.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager

[attachment: customer-draft-omni-1028.txt (text)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:54:02 +0000
Subject: Update: routing exception applied — p95 improving

Update for the thread:

- 09:38 UTC: routing exception to variant-q1 enabled for OmniRetail (route-policy=omni-eu-exception).
- 09:45 UTC: triggered KV cache priming job for tenant prefixes (run id: prime-omni-1028-01).
- 09:52 UTC: observed first steady decline in p95; at 09:54 UTC p95 is ~520ms and QPS recovered to ~95% of baseline.
- Attached: fallback-decision-notes.md (short ops log) and snapshot logs (OPS-4512).

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: during the rollout the kernel scheduler favored new batch-sizes causing per-request latency variance and evicted hot KV entries under memory pressure. We'll own the postmortem; immediate follow-ups:
1) scheduler tuning and a canary throttle to avoid aggressive batch growth.
2) KV cache TTL adjustments and proactive warmup on variant deploys.
3) postmortem + remediation plan targeted for EOD.

I'll keep monitoring and will post once p95 is stable for 30 minutes.

Karthik

[attachment: fallback-decision-notes.md (markdown)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@omni-retail.com>
Cc: Sabrina Chen <sabrina.chen@omni-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 12:03:20 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Update: routing exception applied — OmniRetail EU latency incident (short note)

Alex / Sabrina — forwarding the brief update and next steps from our ops team. TL;DR: we identified a regression tied to a variant rollout in eu-west-1 that caused cache evaporation and scheduler-induced latency growth. We applied an emergency routing exception and cache priming; p95 has returned to ~500ms and throughput is recovering.

What we are doing next:
- Root cause analysis and remediation plan; we will share a short postmortem by EOD today.
- A temporary goodwill credit of 5% will be applied to October usage invoices as a first step; if you want to discuss different remediation we can escalate.
- We will schedule a 30-minute review with our SRE lead and product by Friday to go over technical fixes and controls to prevent recurrence.

Apologies for the interruption — we know latency at checkout is unacceptable and we appreciate your patience. Marissa will follow up with formal billing details.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
